title: Late Fees on Credit Builder Accounts: When a Late Fee Is Owed and How It Is Booked
content:
## When a late fee is owed

A late fee on a Credit Builder account is owed for the account's oldest unpaid due date once its grace period has ended with that installment still unpaid. A Credit Builder late fee is charged at most once per due date, only for the account's oldest unpaid due date and only on an account in active status.

For a late due date with no more than one debit card payment credited toward it, and only for such a due date, the amount of the late fee is figured as the Credit Builder Accounts late-fee policy sets out rather than as a flat percentage of the monthly payment. Every other late due date remains under the earlier fee clause, which for those due dates reads: the late fee is the plan's late-fee percent of the monthly payment, rounded to the cent and not more than the plan's late-fee maximum, at most the plan's maximum number of late fees per due date, and only on an account in active status.

A later due date that lapses while an older installment is still unpaid carries no late fee of its own, so no installment is charged a late fee only because an earlier one is unpaid; once the older installment is paid, the later due date becomes the oldest unpaid due date and its late fee is figured then.

The late due date is the account's oldest unpaid due date, the next due date the account shows, and the late fee is figured for it.

| Account facts | Late fee for that due date |
|---|---|
| active account, oldest unpaid due date past its grace period, installment still unpaid, no late fee yet for that due date | owed |
| the oldest unpaid due date already carries its late fee | not owed again |
| a later due date has lapsed while an older one is still unpaid | none for the later due date while the older one is unpaid |
| account not in active status | not charged |

## Booking a late fee: `assess_late_fee_fbf509e1`

**What it does.** The tool charges one late fee to a Credit Builder account for one missed due date. It books a late-fee entry on the borrower's Credit Builder account, dated today and tied to the due date it is charged for, and adds the fee to the account's unpaid fees. The borrower sees the new late fee and the higher unpaid-fee balance on the account.

**How it is invoked.** It is an agent-side tool: the agent unlocks `assess_late_fee_fbf509e1` and then calls it.

**Parameters.**

| Parameter | Meaning and format |
|---|---|
| `builder_account_id` | reference number of the Credit Builder account being charged, as returned by the Credit Builder account lookup |
| `installment_due_date` | the payment due date the late fee is charged for, written as YYYY-MM-DD (calendar date, no time zone), exactly as it appears on the account record |
| `late_fee_amount` | the late fee to charge in USD, a positive amount with 2 decimal places, already rounded to the cent; the tool stores it rounded to 2 decimal places |

**Return.** A confirmation of the form "Late fee <entry reference> of <amount> USD booked on <account reference> for due date <YYYY-MM-DD>; unpaid fees now <amount> USD.", where the entry reference is the new fee entry's reference number, amounts are in USD with 2 decimal places and the unpaid-fee figure includes this fee. Receiving this text means the fee is on the account.
